This exceeds the 'Scope section spans more than three distinct implementation areas' oversized indicator, and the task's own title, naming 'steps 0-13' (fourteen sequential stages), matches the check's own 'title implies multiple sequential phases' oversizing pattern. tasks.md's own Global Constraints 'Task-decomposition note' records round-1's finding as '12+ pipeline stages plus five new test suites in one unit of work' and round-2's finding as 'T-002 still bundled the entire undivided 12+-stage engine with two full TDD suites' -- but round-2's actual remedy (isolating the twelve-fixture block suite into T-003) left the underlying fourteen-step engine exactly as undivided as after round 1; the note itself states isolating the match suite too 'was deliberately rejected, since it would leave T-002 with no test suite of its own', showing the engine's own scope was never itself reconsidered, only which suite stays attached to it. This is the feature's single Risk: high, Required Workflow: tdd task whose own Risk Rationale states a defect here 'defeats decision document v2 section19's own [Block-on-ambiguity] governing rule' -- the highest-consequence task in the decomposition remains also the largest, unreduced by either remedy round, and is unlikely to be completable in a single focused session (the check's own sizing standard).

T-003 and T-004 both edit the identical shared files (tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 and the staged specs/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml candidate) with no Blockers relationship between them (T-003 Blockers: T-002; T-004 Blockers: T-002 -- neither lists the other), yet both explicitly claim the identical insertion point: T-003's own Planned Files/Scope state its CI steps are 'appended after T-002's own', and T-004's own Planned Files/Scope use the same phrase, 'appended after T-002's own' / 'appending to T-002's own staged candidate'. Per tasks.md's own Global Constraints ('Test-suite/CI-registration serialization, T-001 to T-002 to T-003 to T-004 to T-006 to T-007 to T-008 ... in that exact order'), T-004 should append after T-003's own contribution, not T-002's -- the two tasks' own text is self-contradictory about who appends where in the same shared staged file, with no Blockers field to resolve the ordering. This is exactly the 'uncoordinated parallel scope overlap (both tasks claim to modify the same file with no blocking relationship)' the check defines as a Major finding; the 'legitimate multi-task scope sharing... provided the Blockers field enforces the ordering' exception does not apply since the Blockers field does not enforce it here.

tasks.md's own Global Constraints declares a mandatory shared-file registration order for tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 and the staged human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml candidate: T-001 to T-002 to T-003 to T-004 to T-006 to T-007 to T-008 (T-005 excluded, since 'T-005 registers no new suite'). Computing each task's transitive Blockers closure shows three of the seven required consecutive-pair dependencies are missing, each with the dependent task's own Scope text presupposing the omitted task's prior output: (1) T-004 (Blockers: T-002 only; transitive closure {T-001, T-002}) omits T-003, even though T-004's own Scope claims to append 'to T-002's own staged candidate' -- contradicting the declared T-003-before-T-004 order and leaving T-004's own Done When ('the staged .github/workflows/test.yml candidate carries this task's own three suites' steps appended after T-002's own') unsatisfiable if T-003 has already run first, as the declared order requires; (2) T-006 (Blockers: T-001, T-005; transitive closure {T-001, T-002, T-003, T-005}) omits T-004, even though T-006's own Scope explicitly states its CI append lands 'appended after T-004's own (the last suite-owning task before this one)'; (3) T-008 (Blockers: T-002, T-005, T-006; transitive closure {T-001, T-002, T-003, T-005, T-006}) omits T-007, even though T-008's own Scope states its CI append lands 'appended after T-007's own (the final entry in this feature's own staged candidate)'. Each omission is a missing blocker whose own task text depends on the omitted task's prior output to the shared staged file/MANIFEST.sha256, and whose absence would let the two tasks run out of the declared order, corrupting the staged CI-registration file's own ordering or producing a MANIFEST.sha256 entry a downstream task's own Done When cannot verify. Round 2's own remedy (tasks.md Global Constraints 'Task-decomposition note') fixed the analogous gap for T-007, which now correctly cites T-002/T-003/T-004/T-005/T-006 as Blockers, but did not extend the identical fix to T-004, T-006, or T-008, which retain the same class of gap in the same shared-file serialization chain.
